g0.rationale: THE COHORT'S OPEN G0 QUESTION, RESOLVED AGAINST THE CHARTER'S ASSUMPTION. §2.2's five-step test run verbatim on the frozen directions. STEP 1 — authoritative directions located: 'Als Spülung (für sofortige Regeneration): ins gewaschene, nasse Haar einmassieren, kurz einwirken lassen (ca. 30 Sekunden) und gut ausspülen. Als Kur (für Tiefenregeneration): ins gewaschene, nasse Haar einmassieren, 2-3 Minuten einwirken lassen und genießen, dann ausspülen.' STEP 2 — test each stated mode against §2.1. Mode A 'Als Spülung': after cleansing YES ('ins gewaschene, nasse Haar'); stated contact time YES (ca. 30 Sekunden); rinse YES ('gut ausspülen'); but the mode is self-labelled a Spülung, i.e. a conditioner, and §2.1's category definition requires a rinse-out INTENSIVE TREATMENT (Haarkur/Maske). Mode A is a conditioner mode. Mode B 'Als Kur': after cleansing YES (identical wording); stated contact time YES (2–3 Minuten); rinse YES ('dann ausspülen'); self-labelled a Kur and explicitly purposed 'für Tiefenregeneration'. Mode B IS a qualifying rinse-out mask mode. STEP 3 — exactly one mode qualifies as a MASK mode → classify only that mode, record multi_use: true, name the uncovered mode. STEP 4 not reached (a mode does qualify). STEP 5 not reached: the directions are NOT ambiguous about which mode carries which dwell — the modes are separately named, separately purposed, and carry distinct stated contact times — so `multi_use_directions_ambiguity` does NOT fire. Charter F1 is what governs, and F1's own text says a multi-use product is eligible 'when authoritative directions state a distinct rinse-out mask mode with dwell'. These directions do exactly that.
evidenceSignals: directions mode B verbatim: 'Als Kur (für Tiefenregeneration): ins gewaschene, nasse Haar einmassieren, 2-3 Minuten einwirken lassen und genießen, dann ausspülen'
directions mode A verbatim: 'Als Spülung (für sofortige Regeneration): … kurz einwirken lassen (ca. 30 Sekunden) und gut ausspülen'

the two modes are separately named ('Als Spülung' / 'Als Kur'), separately purposed ('sofortige Regeneration' / 'Tiefenregeneration'), and carry distinct contact times — they are separable, so §2.2 step 5 is not reached
charter F2 (binding): dwell is protocol metadata under P5 and is NEVER a boundary test, so the shortness of either mode cannot decide eligibility
charter F1: eligible when authoritative directions state a distinct rinse-out mask mode with dwell

conditioningLevel.derivation: S1 = NOT satisfied (one cationic). S2 = satisfied (Cetearyl Alcohol @2). S3 = satisfied (Cetyl Esters @5 + Avena Sativa Kernel Oil @11, two distinct non-fatty-alcohol lipids above the tail). Count = 2 of 3.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `high` on the rule as written: ≥2 of {S1,S2,S3} with no material counter-signal. None of §9.1's three enumerated counter-signals applies — there is no rheology-only content, the list is short rather than long, and there is no sub-1% hero tail (the tail holds only Parfum and Vanillin).

`moderate` does not apply on the rule as written: two signals are satisfied, not one. I considered refusing `high` the way I did for #02, on an architecture-level counter-signal, and declined: unlike #02 this IS a conventional aqueous emulsion with water at rank 1, and the two credited lipids are genuinely above the marker. There is no principled architectural reason to override the count here — only an intuition that a fourteen-ingredient 2in1 should not sit at the top of the conditioning scale. Recording that intuition as a rule finding is more useful than silently acting on it.
`low` does not apply: S2 and S3 both hold.

Confidence is capped at `moderate` on two grounds: S3 rests on Avena Sativa Kernel Oil at tail_index − 1 (the lexicon §0.2 boundary-band caution, applied per this lane's policy as a confidence modifier only), and the alternative chelator reading of the tail marker (AP-12-CHELATOR) would remove S3 entirely and drop the value to `moderate`.
counterSignals: S3 is carried by a wax ester at rank 5 and a plant oil at rank 11 — the thinnest lipid evidence to satisfy S3 anywhere in the cohort, against #10's four-lipid block or #05's six.

The whole value hinges on two independent judgment calls: that Cetyl Esters counts as a lipid rather than a fatty alcohol (it does, per lexicon family 2), and that Tetrasodium Glutamate Diacetate is not a tail marker (AP-12-CHELATOR).
limitations: A three-step concentration scale is at the edge of INCI support, and §18 open question 2 asks whether S1/S2/S3 produce a usable spread on the real shelf. This product answers that the failure mode is not collapse to `moderate` but inflation to `high` on thin evidence. See AP-12-HIGHFLOOR.
Downstream, this value projects to `concentration: high` for a product the charter describes as conditioner-engine territory.

adjudicationPoints.title: The charter's own conditioner-mode-only exclusion example is eligible under the charter's own test — ESCALATION TO NICK
adjudicationPoints.body: This is the cohort's designated open G0 question and it resolves against the charter. The charter twice names Guhl Panthenol + Reparatur 2in1 as excluded on the ground that its only rinse-out mode is a short conditioner mode, and §2.1's Excluded list repeats it. The frozen directions show two rinse-out modes: 'Als Spülung … ca. 30 Sekunden' and 'Als Kur (für Tiefenregeneration) … 2-3 Minuten'. Run through F1's five-step test, the Kur mode satisfies every §2.1 conjunct that any other cohort product satisfies, and F2 forbids dwell from acting as a boundary test — so a 2–3 minute Kur cannot be refused for being short when the charter admits 7-second and 30-second Kuren by name. Exactly one mode qualifies as an INTENSIVE treatment (the Spülung mode is self-labelled a conditioner), so §2.2 step 3 applies and step 5's ambiguity branch is not reached. Result: eligible, mode-scoped. I have classified it and flagged it; it must not be silently adopted. The choice for Nick is between correcting the charter's example (accepting that a 2in1 Kur & Spülung with a stated Kur mode is a mask in that mode) and adding an explicit label-based rule that keeps Kur-und-Spülung 2in1 products in Conditioner-engine territory regardless of the five-step test. The second preserves his evident intent but requires the charter to say that mode LABELLING overrides the directions test for this product shape — a real narrowing of F1 that should be written down rather than left as an example.
adjudicationPoints.source: charter F1 and Known boundary cases; §2.1 Excluded list; §2.2 five-step test; cohort openG0Question

adjudicationPoints.title: The S1/S2/S3 count gives the cohort's lightest formula a `high` conditioning level
adjudicationPoints.body: A fourteen-ingredient silicone-free 2in1 with one cationic, one fatty alcohol, one wax ester and one oat oil satisfies S2 and S3 and therefore scores `high` — the same value as #10's four-lipid, two-cationic butter mask and #04's three-cationic bond mask. §18 open question 2 asked whether the counting rule produces a usable spread or collapses to `moderate`; this cohort's answer is that it does neither cleanly. It produced five `high`, five `moderate` and zero `low` across twelve products, and the `high` bucket contains both the richest and the lightest formulas in the set. The specific defect is that S3 needs only two distinct non-fatty-alcohol lipids of any weight class at any above-tail rank, so a wax ester at rank 5 plus a plant oil at tail_index − 1 counts the same as a shea-plus-coconut block at ranks 4 and 5. Candidate fixes: weight S3 by lipid class (require at least one R4b, or two R4a within the first eight above-tail ranks); require S1 to be among the satisfied signals for `high` (see AP-06-NOCATIONIC); or accept a two-step scale, which evidence §2 says is closer to what INCI can support.

adjudicationPoints.title: The standard and the lexicon disagree about whether chelators are tail-class, and neither list covers this product's chelator
adjudicationPoints.body: §3.1's tail-class enumeration includes a 'trace chelators' category listing five species. The lexicon §0.2's tail_marker definition includes fragrance, allergens, preservatives and colourants — and no chelators at all. This product declares Tetrasodium Glutamate Diacetate at rank 7, a common chelator on neither list. Reading §3.1's enumeration as closed, it is not a marker and tail_index is 12 (Phenoxyethanol). Reading it as illustrative, tail_index is 7, the credited segment shrinks from eleven entries to six, S3 fails, and conditioning_level drops from `high` to `moderate` — which happens to be the value AP-12-HIGHFLOOR argues is more honest. Two documents that disagree on a rule this load-bearing should be reconciled before the blind lane is scored; and whichever way it goes, the chelator list needs to be explicitly closed or explicitly open.
